title: Dependency Rules & Circular Dependencies
objectives: Draw the allowed dependency graph between features, shared and domain

examples.name: rules.txt
examples.code:
allowed:
  feature  -> shared, domain, api
  store    -> domain, api
  shared   -> (nothing internal)

forbidden:
  shared   -> feature
  domain   -> feature, store
  featureA -> featureB (prefer events/router/stores)

exercise.prompt: Two features need the same helper. Which option avoids coupling? Render the ranking: "duplicate the helper", "move it to shared/", "import across features", "make it a domain module if it is business logic".
hints: Cross-feature imports couple release cycles; shared/ or domain/ decouples.
Duplication is sometimes cheaper than the wrong shared abstraction.

questions.prompt: A imports B and B imports A. The first fix to try is…
options: extract the shared part into a lower module both may import
make both import each other conditionally
questions.explanation: Cycles break by pulling the mutually-needed code down into shared/ or domain/.

options: a coupling hub that erodes the architecture
questions.explanation: Upward imports from shared/ recreate the coupling the layer was built to prevent.
